primaryBusiness:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril Intelligence Systems (AIS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Intelligence Community (IC) customers. We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are looking for a Head of Operations to join our rapidly growing Intelligence Systems team. In this role you will be responsible for all business operations for the business line you support. Your work will vary from quick-turn operational fire-fighting, to building and redesigning processes, to leading high-impact strategic projects. This role requires you to be a trusted partner to each part of the business, and to work with and support the Division leadership teams to achieve our strategic objectives.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 
 Partner to the GM — Serve as the right hand to the General Manager of Intelligence Systems, responsible for all internal operations of the business line.

 Act as COO of the business line — Drive day-to-day business operations for Intelligence Systems. This includes business planning & organization design, financial tracking, talent planning & people operations, staffing and hiring, corporate governance, go-to-market, real estate & facility planning, security & infrastructure compliance, proposal & legal support, and sharing the division's narrative — working with cross-functional partners across each of these domains.

 Lead the BizOps team — Lead the Business Operations team within Intelligence Systems, composed of a Business Execution/Services team and Business Analytics, with the potential to include Production Operations/Analytics.

 Own the bottom line — Own the business line P&L and burn rate. Partner with Finance and FP&A to track financial health against division goals, take action to keep operating expenses within budget, and recommend strategies to drive toward margin targets.

 Define growth strategy — Define the growth strategy for Intelligence Systems in partnership with the Intelligence Systems Leadership Team, and lead strategic initiatives in line with business line priorities.

 Enable the engineering mission — Support the growth, execution, and engineering of the business line with operational support.

 Scale the organization — Problem solve to enable the business line to operate as efficiently as possible and scale accordingly.

 Represent the business externally — Build senior leader engagement and external interface strategy (e.g., conferences, press releases, partnerships).

 Build partnerships — Build, negotiate, and execute partnerships across industry.

 Support M&A activity — Identify targets and engage in diligence.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 10-15+ years of professional experience in operations.

 Strong communication skills; trusted by executives and colleagues alike — Demonstrated ability to translate and articulate thoughts clearly and simply across a wide range of roles (software engineers, finance partners, recruiters, cross-functional leadership, and executives). Communications excellence across a wide dynamic range, both written and verbal. Experience interfacing with company leadership and executives is a must, with a demonstrated ability to cultivate trust, facilitate meetings for, and engage with executives.

 Technically minded — Solid technical aptitude and proven ability to understand technical designs, and the ability to work closely and effectively with engineering teams.

 Bridges operational and analytical teams — Strong emotional intelligence and ability to solve operational problems in a way that is both data-driven and people-centric.

 High ownership and capacity — Horsepower to effectively manage multiple (6+) large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.

 Finance literate — Comfortable owning a bottom line, reading and acting on P&L, budget, and margin data in partnership with FP&A.

 Ability to work onsite five days a week at either our Reston, VA office or our HQ in Costa Mesa, CA.

 Minimum 25% travel expected.

 Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 MBA or similar degree.

 Experience working with engineers and bringing hardware/software products to market strongly preferred.

 Experience in the intelligence community or national security mission space

 Experience leading a business operations, business analytics, or similar function

 Experience working effectively in a matrix organization structure.

 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Finance, or a related field.

 US Salary Range
 $183,000 — $243,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 

 

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

 

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


 

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ . 

 

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

primaryBusiness:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is building the infrastructure that powers the AI revolution. As our global footprint expands across data centers, power generation, manufacturing, construction sites, and corporate offices — and as the visibility of our executives and the stakes of our operations continue to rise — the ability to protect our people wherever the business takes them is increasingly critical.

The Senior Manager, Protective Operations will lead Crusoe's executive protection and protective operations programs globally, providing risk-based protection for executives, employees, travelers, and company operations. You will serve as the company's subject matter expert for executive protection, travel risk, protective intelligence, threat management, and sensitive security investigations.

This role will join Crusoe's growing Physical Security organization at a formative moment. You will shape the standards, protocols, vendor network, and operating rhythm that supports Crusoe's expanding global footprint — working closely with the GSOC, the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst, People, Legal, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, and business leaders to identify risk and translate intelligence into effective protective measures.

The ideal candidate brings experience from U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, high-end executive protection, special operations, or protective details at the national or diplomatic level, and has translated that tradecraft into corporate Protective Operations leadership. You know how to protect people without unnecessarily disrupting the business, and you know how to lead a program that scales.



What You'll Be Working On:

Executive Protection Program Leadership

 - Lead Crusoe's global Executive Protection program, including executive travel, residential considerations, ground transportation, advance work, event coverage, and protective operations

 - Develop risk-based protection strategies based on threat, exposure, location, activity, and other relevant factors rather than title alone

 - Lead security planning for executive appearances, media engagements, conferences, town halls, board activities, major company events, and other high-profile engagements

 - Establish and maintain the standards, protocols, and tradecraft discipline expected of a world-class corporate protection program

Travel Risk Management

 - Own the Travel Risk Management program, establishing processes for pre-travel risk assessment, traveler briefings, high-risk travel, escalation, emergency support, and traveler assistance

 - Conduct advance work and security assessments for domestic and international travel, including hotels, venues, transportation, routes, medical capabilities, and contingency planning

 - Build the duty-of-care framework and escalation procedures that protect Crusoe travelers wherever the business sends them

Protective Intelligence Partnership

 - Partner closely with the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst and the GSOC to translate protective intelligence into protective action — movement planning, principal protection decisions, advance planning, and threat response

 - Shape the intelligence requirements and collection priorities that support protective operations

 - Operationalize protective intelligence products into daily decisions, travel decisions, and event planning

Threat Assessment and Management

 - Establish and support threat assessment and management processes for workplace violence, threatening communications, stalking, harassment, fixated individuals, concerning behavior, and other potential threats

 - Partner with HR, Employee Relations, Legal, and the Intelligence Analyst on threat cases requiring coordinated response and protective action

 - Apply structured behavioral threat assessment methodologies to differentiate legitimate threats from noise

Sensitive Security Investigations

 - Lead or support sensitive security investigations involving threats, theft, misconduct, unauthorized access, insider risk, security incidents, and suspected fraud in partnership with Legal, People, Internal Audit, Information Security, and other stakeholders

 - Support elevated-risk employee matters, including sensitive terminations, credible threats, domestic violence concerns affecting the workplace, and other situations requiring additional protective measures

 - Maintain investigative discipline, chain of custody, and reporting standards appropriate to the sensitivity of each matter

Site and Geographic Risk Assessment

 - Conduct geographic and site security risk assessments in support of new markets, potential company locations, major projects, and business expansion

 - Evaluate country, city, neighborhood, and site-level risks including crime, political instability, civil unrest, terrorism, emergency response, medical capabilities, transportation, natural hazards, and other relevant threats

 - Produce assessments that inform executive travel, site selection, event planning, and business expansion decisions

Program Development and Vendor Management

 - Develop protective operations plans, standards, protocols, and escalation procedures that scale across a growing global organization

 - Select, manage, and evaluate executive protection, secure transportation, travel security, investigative, and other specialized security vendors globally

 - Grow the vendor network — domestic and international — required to extend Crusoe's protective capabilities wherever the business operates

 - Support budget development, forecasting, and financial management for protective operations programs and vendors

Operational Partnership

 - Coordinate closely with the GSOC during executive travel, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents

 - Establish relationships with law enforcement, government agencies, security partners, and other external organizations relevant to protective operations

 - Support crisis and incident response involving executives, employees, travelers, threats, or other security events

Program Measurement and Maturity

 - Develop metrics and reporting to measure program effectiveness, emerging risks, protective activity, and opportunities for improvement

 - Help mature the Protective Operations function as Crusoe's global footprint and risk profile continue to evolve

 - Maintain discretion and sound judgment when handling highly sensitive executive, employee, investigative, and company information



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 10+ years of experience in executive protection, corporate security, protective intelligence, law enforcement, military protective operations, diplomatic security, or a related field

 - 5+ years leading complex executive protection, protective operations, or corporate security programs

 - Demonstrated experience protecting senior executives and supporting domestic and international travel

 - Strong experience conducting advances, threat assessments, security risk assessments, and protective planning

 - Experience developing and managing executive protection programs in a corporate environment strongly preferred

 - Knowledge of protective intelligence, behavioral threat assessment, workplace violence prevention, and threat management principles

 - Experience conducting or managing sensitive corporate or security investigations

 - Understanding of travel risk management, including international security environments, traveler risk assessment, emergency response, and duty-of-care considerations

 - Experience planning security for media engagements, executive appearances, major events, and other high-profile activities

 - Ability to assess rapidly evolving situations, make sound risk-based decisions, and operate effectively with incomplete information

 - Demonstrated ability to work with senior executives while maintaining discretion, professionalism, adaptability, and confidentiality

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate risk and recommendations to executives and business leaders

 - Experience managing specialized security vendors, executive protection providers, secure transportation providers, and other external partners

 - Ability to collaborate effectively across Legal, People, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, Operations, and other business functions

 - Ability to travel domestically and internationally approximately 30–50%, with periods of increased travel based on operational requirements

 - Ability to respond outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support



Bonus Points

 - Prior service with U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, FBI, DEA, U.S. Marshals Service, or an equivalent federal protective agency

 - Military special operations background with protective detail experience (SOF, MARSOC, Naval Special Warfare, Air Force Special Tactics, or equivalent)

 - Prior corporate executive protection leadership experience within technology, critical infrastructure, data centers, energy, manufacturing, or another rapidly growing global organization

 - Experience leading principal-level protective details for Fortune 500 CEOs, founders, or high-net-worth principals

 - Experience developing enterprise Travel Risk Management or Workplace Violence Prevention programs

 - Experience conducting protective intelligence and open-source threat research

 - Experience supporting international operations and higher-risk travel environments, including gray and amber travel zones

 - Experience working with law enforcement, intelligence, diplomatic, or government security organizations

 - Familiarity with intelligence, case management, mass notification, travel risk, and security operations platforms (Ontic, Dataminr, Everbridge, International SOS, Crisis24, or peer tools)

 - CPP, PSP, PCI, Certified Threat Manager (CTM), ATAP certifications, or other relevant professional credentials

 - Multilingual capability, particularly in languages supporting Crusoe's international footprint



OPERATING CONDITIONS:

 - San Francisco or Denver on-site, with domestic and international travel of approximately 30–50% to support executive protection, advance work, high-risk travel, site assessments, and major events

 - On-call availability for executive travel windows, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents

 - Response outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support

 - Occasional nights, weekends, and holidays as the operational tempo demands

 - Handling of sensitive, confidential, and executive-protection information with appropriate discretion is a core expectation of the role


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

Success in this role means Crusoe has a proactive, intelligence-led, and risk-based protective operations program capable of supporting executives and employees wherever the business operates.

You will lead a program that identifies threats early, provides executives and travelers with appropriate protection without unnecessarily disrupting business, responds effectively to sensitive incidents, and scales as Crusoe expands into new markets and operating environments.

You will also establish a close operating partnership with the GSOC and the Intelligence Analyst: the GSOC maintains global situational awareness and enterprise threat monitoring, the Intelligence Analyst produces protective intelligence assessments, and Protective Operations owns the translation of intelligence into protective action.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 - $260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




ABOUT THIS ROLE



The Director, Commercial Operations will be the operational backbone of Crusoe's Energy Development Group. This person owns the analytical frameworks, pipeline processes, and team capabilities that allow Crusoe to evaluate and advance land and power opportunities at speed and at scale. From complex financial modeling and market analysis to pipeline integrity and board-level reporting, this role ensures the BD team operates with precision and strategic clarity.

This is a leadership-first, analytically grounded role. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in energy project finance or development, a track record of building and mentoring high-performing analyst teams, and the process orientation to continuously raise the quality bar on how Crusoe evaluates and advances opportunities. You will work closely with senior leadership across Energy Development, Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams and will be a key contributor to the operational health of Crusoe's project pipeline.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON



 - Overseeing a team of Energy Development Analysts, setting the standard for analytical rigor, process discipline, and professional growth

 - Owning the development and refinement of economic models that underpin power origination and data center site pricing decisions

 - Driving continuous improvement of due diligence workflows, pipeline management processes, and reporting mechanisms across the Energy Development team

 - Overseeing the integrity and accuracy of Crusoe's data center opportunity pipeline, ensuring leadership has a reliable, real-time view of the project portfolio

 - Supervising the creation of board-level presentations, project approval materials, and executive communications that translate analytical complexity into clear strategic recommendations

 - Tracking and synthesizing hyperscaler activity, regulatory developments, and domestic energy infrastructure trends to surface actionable intelligence for the team

 - Supporting cross-functional collaboration between Energy Development and the Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams to move projects efficiently through the development pipeline






CORE RESPONSIBILITIES



Lead and enable the Energy Development Analyst team

 - Support, mentor, and develop a team of analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture

 - Provide hands-on guidance on financial modeling, market analysis, and project evaluation

Drive analytical quality and strategic relevance

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. About This Role

Crusoe is seeking an experienced and proactive DC Operations & Deployments EHS Safety Manager to join our expanding team. This new role, based in our San Francisco office, will be an integral member of the Global Safety Pillar, reporting directly to the Senior Director of Global Safety, supporting deployments, data center operations, and R&D projects. You will be crucial in establishing and continuously improving HSE performance, processes, and culture throughout our physical infrastructure operations. The ideal candidate will possess a foundational understanding of safety programs combined with exceptional communications and collaboration skills to drive safety initiatives. This is a full-time position.

 

What You’ll Be Working On

 - On-Site Safety Leadership: Provide dedicated safety oversight for active deployments and operational data centers, serving as the primary safety point of contact for internal teams and external contractors

 - Risk Assessment and Mitigation: Assess risks to workers, making recommendations and developing action plans to reduce risk as appropriate.

 - HSE Program Development: Develop and implement various HSE processes, including Right to Know policies and Hazard Communication programs to support a safe and compliant work environment.

 - Incident Management: Facilitate thorough incident investigations and lead root cause analysis efforts following any failures, incidents, or accidents. You will actively monitor and follow up on the status of corrective actions, reports, and audits.

 - Training and Culture: Develop and maintain a high level of HSE awareness and culture through communications, training, and promoting active involvement in HSE programs. You will coordinate and actively participate in the HSE training of personnel.

 - Stakeholder/Regulatory Liaison: Liaise effectively with local contractors, clients, local agencies and air quality boards regarding HSE issues, ensuring open and clear communication.

 - Documentation Management: Ensure that the relevant HSE documentation such as MSDS/SDS folders are meticulously maintained, up to date and readily available at the worksites.

 - Technical Knowledge: Proven technical knowledge of various HSE rules and regulations at both the Federal and State levels. Direct experience with the implementation of HSE rules, regulations, policies, and procedures is a must.

 - Communication Skills: Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective collaboration and reporting.

 - Legal Work Status: Candidates must be able to legally work and reside in the US without requiring sponsorship.

 - Travel Requirements: 50% Travel Required

primaryBusiness:
Quindar builds software to manage satellites like servers. We are seeking a Vice President of Operations to build the operating system, organizational infrastructure, and business processes that turn company strategy into execution as we scale across commercial and government markets.

This leader owns business operations, strategy and performance, facilities, and General & Administrative functions. Beyond running the operating cadence, the role connects corporate strategy, resource allocation, and cross-functional execution so that Quindar consistently makes the right investments and turns them into business outcomes. The role holds the authority to resolve cross-functional prioritization conflicts at the leadership level, with clear and intentional escalation to the CEO, while functional leaders retain accountability for their results and authority over their teams.

Facilities, Business Operations, and the G&A team report to this role, with their leaders responsible for day-to-day execution. This is a hands-on executive role for someone who can build a function, develop its leaders, and drive execution across the company.



Company Execution and Performance Management

• Translate company strategy into company OKRs and functional commitments with accountable owners, deadlines, dependencies, and approved resources.

• Agree with each functional leader on a small set of meaningful KPIs with clear definitions, source data, targets, and reporting frequency, and maintain a consolidated performance dashboard across Sales, Product, Engineering, Programs, Finance, People and Brand, and Operations.

• Design and run the company operating model: quarterly planning, leadership reviews, decision tracking, and follow-up, with a visible record of commitments delivered, missed, corrected, and rescoped.

• Design and implement a company-wide model for cross-functional prioritization and decision-making at the leadership level, including decision rights and escalation paths, aligned with and actively reinforced by the CEO.

• Use the operating data to drive decisions and corrective actions, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and escalate decisions that put company goals at risk.

• Partner with functional leaders and the VP of Finance to align workforce capacity, hiring plans, facilities, and budgets with company priorities.



Corporate Strategy and Go-to-Market

• Help shape corporate strategy with the CEO and leadership team, including evaluating markets and opportunities, defining investment requirements, and translating strategic choices into resourced plans.

• Lead the cross-functional planning and execution of GTM priorities in partnership with the CEO, who leads Sales & Marketing: align Product, Engineering, Programs, and Operations behind revenue priorities and ensure the organization is resourced to deliver them.

• Lead the evaluation and incubation of new business opportunities, including, but not limited to,Operations as a Service (OaaS). For OaaS, lead the initial cross-functional effort to take the offering from concept toward launch, including the business model, service definition and commercial terms, investment requirements, and operational readiness.

• Ensure new services, markets, and programs are integrated into company planning, performance management, and compliance from the outset.



AI-Enabled Business Operations

• Lead the AI Business Operations team to build and deploy workflows that reduce manual coordination and increase output across Quindar, with measurable reductions in hands-on processing time and sustained adoption.

• Identify and baseline the highest-value workflows across functions, prioritizing those that remove coordination overhead between Product, Engineering, Programs, Sales, and Marketing (for example, specifications to engineering tickets, user documentation, marketing materials, and proposal development).

• Build internal knowledge infrastructure, such as a company data warehouse of product knowledge, engineering designs, documentation, and marketing and proposal content, that any role can query or use to create collateral through an agentic interface.

• Implement appropriate access controls, source traceability, and compliance requirements, including CUI handling, before any workflow handling sensitive or consequential outputs enters production use.



Facilities and Classified Readiness

• Own facilities planning, buildouts, workplace operations, vendor management, and procurement across all unclassified and classified spaces.

• Maintain an integrated master schedule covering construction, procurement, vendors, budget, and readiness for each space, with a defined risk and impact scale, reviewed regularly with the CEO.

• Deliver the facilities infrastructure needed for classified readiness, completing facilities work ahead of accreditation target dates and obtaining Security’s written acceptance against an agreed readiness checklist.

• Partner with Security, IT, Contracts, and program leadership so that facilities, policies, training, and records support classified program and audit requirements. Security retains accreditation responsibility.



General and Administrative Operations

• Lead legal operations, and corporate administrative services through internal teams and outside partners.

• Manage outside counsel and coordinate corporate legal matters, employment matters, contract review, and company policies.

• Own cap table and stock option administration in partnership with Finance and legal counsel, and maintain corporate records and board and stockholder approval workflows with the CEO and counsel.

• Own the administrative infrastructure required to pursue and support government business, including SAM.gov http://SAM.gov registration, applicable NSTXL and consortium memberships, JCP certification/DD Form 2345, and a centralized calendar of registrations, renewals, and reporting obligations.

• Oversee export compliance program administration, including applicable ITAR/EAR processes, working with qualified counsel and designated compliance personnel.

• Coordinate corporate insurance, business continuity planning, corporate overhead efficiency, and company-wide operational risk management.



Fundraising and Finance Partnership

• Lead operational, legal, people, and corporate diligence readiness for fundraising alongside the VP of Finance, including an organized data room and timely, accurate responses to investor requests.

• Support board materials and investor reporting with company operating metrics, organizational plans, and progress against strategic priorities.

• Partner with Finance on operating plans, overhead budgets, and the investments needed to support the next stage of growth and new business lines.



Qualifications

• Experience leading operations at a growing technology company, with exposure to government contracting or another regulated market.

• Demonstrated success building teams, systems, and operating processes through a significant stage of organizational growth.

• Experience contributing to corporate strategy and leading cross-functional GTM or new-business initiatives from concept to launch, with a bias toward revenue and business outcomes.

• Experience across facilities, legal operations, compliance, or business operations.

• A hands-on track record of using AI, technology, and automation to improve operational efficiency.

• Familiarity with venture-backed company governance, equity administration, and fundraising diligence.

• Ability to turn ambiguous priorities into clear plans, coordinate executive peers, and hold teams accountable for commitments.

• Strong judgment about when to act directly, delegate, escalate, or engage specialist expertise.



What Success Looks Like

• Company strategy is reflected in OKRs, KPIs, and commitments with clear owners, and leaders run the business from a trusted, shared dashboard.

• Cross-functional prioritization decisions are made quickly and consistently at the leadership level, with less day-to-day intervention from the CEO.

• GTM priorities and new services such as OaaS move from strategy to resourced, cross-functionally executed plans with measurable revenue impact.

• AI-enabled workflows are in production across functions, materially reducing manual coordination while meeting access-control and compliance requirements.

• Facilities for classified operations are delivered on schedule and accepted by Security.

• Organizational structures, career frameworks, equity programs, and scaling processes are ready ahead of growth to 150+ employees.

• Required registrations, compliance obligations, and corporate and equity records remain current and diligence-ready.



Security Clearance Eligibility Requirement
Due to U.S. Government contractual requirements, this position requires eligibility for a U.S. Government security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance; therefore, candidates for this position must be U.S. citizens. An active clearance is not required at the time of hire but is preferred and may be required in the future based on program needs.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

 - To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.


WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT QUINDAR

 - We work in a cutting edge industry and you will get the opportunity to be part of a small team with a large direct impact on the success of our customers’ space missions!

 - We take work life balance very seriously. We require employees to take 15 days off but provide unlimited PTO and follow most US federal government holidays.

 - Mental health is just as important as physical so we provide quarterly health & wellness benefits.

 - Comprehensive health insurance for you and your family with 100% coverage for employees.

 - We encourage employees to save for retirement and provide 4% 401(k) matching.

 - Each quarter we have a 4-day company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

 - Our culture and company is evolving. You will be key in creating the next major or minor version!
